\section{Overview}
\subsection*{Brief - synchronous buck converter board (sbuck-5v3a)}
Design a synchronous buck converter board.

\subsubsection*{SPECIFICATION}
\begin{itemize}
\item Input:        7-18V DC, nominal 12V, via 2-pin 5.08mm screw terminal
\item Output:       5.0V +/-2\%, 3A continuous, via 2-pin 5.08mm screw terminal
\item Load step:    0 to 3A, recovery within 100us, \textless{}200mV excursion
\item Output ripple: \textless{}50mV pk-pk at full load
\item Efficiency:   \textgreater{}88\% at 12V in, 3A out
\item Ambient:      up to 50C, no forced airflow
\item Protection:   input reverse polarity, output overcurrent, thermal shutdown
\item Board:        \textless{}=50x40mm, 4x M3 mounting holes, 2 or 4 layer (your call, justify it)
\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{PART SELECTION}
\begin{itemize}
\item Prefer an integrated synchronous buck IC over a controller + discrete FETs at
this power level. Candidate families to evaluate: TI TPS54xxx/TPS56xxx, MPS
MP23xx/MP15xx, Diodes AP63xxx, Silergy SY82xx. Do not trust remembered ratings
for any of these - pull the datasheet and confirm Vin range, Iout, and switching
frequency before committing.
\item Verify LCSC stock and basic/extended tier for every part before finalising. A
part that is out of stock is a failed design.
\item Inductor: compute ripple current dI = (Vin - Vout) {*} D / (L {*} fsw), where
D = Vout/Vin. Target 20-40\% of full load current. Size saturation current above
Iout + dI/2 with margin, at temperature, not at 25C. Check DCR against your
efficiency target.
\item Input capacitance: ceramic close-in for the switching loop plus bulk for the
cable inductance. Input cap RMS current is roughly Iout {*} sqrt(D {*} (1-D)) -
check the ceramic's ripple rating and derate MLCC capacitance for DC bias, which
can cost more than half the nameplate value at rated voltage.
\item Output capacitance: ripple is roughly dI/(8 {*} fsw {*} Cout) + dI {*} ESR. Check the
load-step requirement too, which usually sets Cout above what ripple alone needs.
\item Every MLCC needs voltage derating; X7R or X5R only, no Y5V.
\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{SCHEMATIC}
\begin{itemize}
\item Feedback divider sized for the IC's internal reference; keep divider impedance low
enough that FB bias current does not shift the setpoint.
\item Include the bootstrap capacitor, enable/UVLO divider if the IC supports it, and a
soft-start component if it is not internal.
\item Reverse polarity: a P-channel FET in the supply path is more efficient than a
series diode at 3A. Confirm Vgs rating against maximum input voltage.
\item Add an optional RC snubber footprint across the low-side switch, DNP by default.
\item Provide test points for VIN, SW, VOUT, FB, EN, GND, plus a low-inductance scope
ground point near the output.
\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{LAYOUT}
Placement first, routing second. Placement decides this design.

\begin{itemize}
\item The high di/dt loop is input capacitor -\textgreater{} high-side switch -\textgreater{} low-side switch -\textgreater{}
back to the capacitor's ground. Minimise its enclosed area above everything else.
Put the smallest input ceramic directly across the IC's VIN and PGND pins on the
same layer, no vias in that loop.
\item The switch node is the primary radiator. Make its copper large enough to carry
current and conduct heat, and no larger. Do not pour it as a plane.
\item Keep the feedback trace short, away from SW and the inductor body, and tap it from
the output capacitor terminal rather than the inductor pin so it senses the
regulated node.
\item Bootstrap capacitor directly at its pins.
\item Single low-impedance ground reference under the converter. Avoid routing signal
returns through the power ground path. If 4 layer, put an uninterrupted ground
plane on the layer directly under the switching components and do not cut it.
\item Size copper by current using IPC-2152, accounting for the 10-20C rise you can
accept. 1oz outer copper is 35um; check whether inner layers are 0.5oz in the
stackup you pick.
\item Place a via array under the IC's thermal pad and stitch the ground planes together
around the loop.
\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{THERMAL}
\begin{itemize}
\item Estimate dissipation at 12V/3A from the IC's efficiency curve, then check junction
temperature against RthJA for the copper area you actually have, at 50C ambient.
\item Inductor DCR loss is I\textasciicircum{}2 {*} DCR; confirm the part's own temperature rise.
\item If the numbers do not close, increase copper area or change parts. Do not assume
the exposed pad alone is sufficient.
\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{EMI / DFM}
\begin{itemize}
\item Keep the switching loop and SW node away from the board edge and connectors.
\item No unnecessary ground plane splits or slots under the converter.
\item Silkscreen legible, none on pads, polarity and pin 1 marked on every polarised part.
\item Respect JLCPCB's minimum trace/space, annular ring, and hole sizes for the process
class you select. Confirm every footprint's rotation against JLCPCB's CPL
convention, not the KiCad default.
\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{BEFORE DECLARING DONE}
1. DRC and ERC clean, zero unrouted nets. 2. Recompute inductor peak current, input cap RMS current, output ripple, and junction temperature from the parts you actually chose, and state the numbers. 3. Confirm each part is in stock at LCSC with its part number recorded. 4. Report the input loop enclosed area, switch node copper area, feedback trace length, and thermal via count.

\subsubsection*{DECISION POLICY}
Make every remaining decision yourself. Do not ask clarifying questions. Where this brief is silent, take the conventional, conservative option. Record each non-obvious choice in DECISIONS.md with one line of reasoning.

Deliver: schematic, layout, gerbers, BOM, CPL, DECISIONS.md, and the computed numbers above.

\subsubsection*{1. Function}
A standalone, open-frame step-down DC-DC power module: it takes an unregulated 7-18 V DC input (12 V nominal) on a 2-pin screw terminal and produces a regulated 5.0 V +/-2\% output at up to 3 A continuous (15 W) on a second 2-pin screw terminal, using a synchronous buck topology built around an integrated buck IC (internal high-side and low-side switches) rather than a controller plus discrete FETs. The board protects itself and its source against reverse-polarity connection of the input, and protects itself against output overcurrent and over-temperature. There is no MCU, no digital interface, no telemetry, and no sequencing or remote control: the board regulates whenever a valid input is applied. Scope is the converter only.

\subsubsection*{8. Compliance / safety flags}
Applicable:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{High current (\textgreater{}= 3 A).} The output is specified at exactly 3.0 A continuous, which sits
on the brief's own high-current threshold, and the input side draws up to \textasciitilde{}2.6 A at low
line. This is the flag that drives copper sizing (IPC-2152, with the 10-20 C rise the
brief permits), connector current rating, and the fusing question. Per role rules this is
NOT guessed: see Q5 (is 3 A the true worst case, or is there a peak/inrush above it),
Q7 (overcurrent mechanism and whether an input fuse is required) and Q29 (fault behaviour
the board must survive: sustained short circuit on the output).
\item \textbf{Undefined fault energy.} The brief does not state whether the input source is current
limited, so the power available into a fault is unbounded as specified: a 4 A input fuse
at 18 V still passes \textasciitilde{}72 W. Behaviour under a bolted output short, and under a reversed
or swapped input, must be defined rather than assumed - Q7, Q29, Q30.
\item \textbf{Switching EMI.} A hard-switching buck is a deliberate broadband noise source. The brief
imposes layout-level EMI requirements (loop area, SW node away from edges/connectors, no
plane splits) but names no standard - Q31.
\end{itemize}
Not applicable (confirmed against the brief):

\begin{itemize}
\item No mains voltage anywhere on the board. Maximum potential is 18 V.
\item No battery of any chemistry, no charging circuit, no cell balancing.
\item No motors, relays, solenoids or other inductive actuator loads driven by this board.
\item No node above 30 V under normal operation (18 V max input; switch-node ringing must
still be kept below the chosen IC's absolute max, which is a design check, not a
safety-agency flag).
\item No intentional RF transmission.
\end{itemize}
Consequence: no agency-certification path (UL/IEC mains safety, battery transport, RF type approval) applies to this board. The safety work is entirely thermal, fault-current and connector-rating engineering.

\subsubsection*{9. Open questions}
Each has a recommended default. The orchestrator answers all of them at once as delegate, per the brief's DECISION POLICY, and each answer becomes a DECISIONS.md line.

1. {*}{*}Does the +/-2\% output window include ripple and load-step transients, or only DC accuracy?{*}{*} Default: +/-2\% is the DC setpoint over line, load and temperature; the 50 mV ripple and the 200 mV load-step excursion are separate, additional allowances. 2. \textbf{How is the \textless{}50 mV ripple measured?} Default: at the output screw terminal, scope in 20 MHz bandwidth-limited mode with a short spring ground (the standard method) - so high-frequency switching spikes above 20 MHz are excluded from the number. 3. \textbf{How fast is the 0-3 A load step?} Default: 2.5 A/us electronic-load slew (a common bench setting), applied at 12 V in. A faster step would be dominated by output-cap ESL rather than by the control loop. 4. {*}{*}Is the \textgreater{}88\% efficiency measured at the screw terminals (including the reverse-polarity FET and terminal resistance) or across the IC only?{*}{*} Default: terminal to terminal, i.e. the reverse-polarity FET loss counts against the budget. This is the conservative reading. 5. {*}{*}Is 3 A the true worst case, or must the board survive brief peaks above it (e.g. a capacitive or lamp load at turn-on)?{*}{*} Default: 3.0 A is the continuous maximum and the design target; the IC's own current limit is allowed to be the only headroom above it, with the current limit set no lower than 4 A to avoid nuisance foldback. 6. \textbf{Any input surge above 18 V (automotive load dump, hot-plug ringing on a long cable)?} Default: no formal surge requirement, but select the IC and input caps for a minimum 28 V rating (\textgreater{}1.5x the 18 V max) so hot-plug ringing on an inductive cable does not destroy the part. 7. \textbf{Overcurrent protection mechanism, and is an input fuse required?} Default: rely on the buck IC's internal cycle-by-cycle current limit with hiccup-mode short-circuit protection (auto-recovering), AND fit a slow-blow input fuse or PTC sized \textasciitilde{}4 A as a fail-safe against a shorted high-side switch, which the IC cannot protect against. 8. {*}{*}Is the IC's internal thermal shutdown sufficient, or is an independent thermal cutout required?{*}{*} Default: internal TSD is sufficient given the low power and the absence of any agency requirement; no separate thermistor or cutout. 9. \textbf{Screw terminal part and wire entry direction.} Default: 5.08 mm pitch, 2-pin, horizontal (side) wire entry facing outward from the board edge, rated \textgreater{}= 10 A / 300 V, accepting 12-24 AWG; choose whichever LCSC-stocked family (KF128/KF301-class or equivalent) is in stock in quantity with a verified footprint. 10. \textbf{Input and output on opposite board edges, or the same edge?} Default: opposite short edges (input left, output right), giving a straight-through power flow, maximum separation between the noisy input loop and the output terminal, and no chance of a user swapping the two identical connectors... which leads to Q30. 11. \textbf{Any indicator LED?} Default: yes, one low-current green LED on VOUT (\textasciitilde{}1 mA, \textasciitilde{}5 mW), as an at-a-glance "output is live" indicator. Cost to efficiency at 3 A is negligible (0.03\%). Say no if the pure-efficiency reading is preferred. 12. \textbf{Any power-good (PG) output brought out?} Default: no external PG connector; if the chosen IC has a PG pin, bring it to a test pad only. 13. \textbf{Test point physical form.} Default: 1.5 mm bare round SMD pads for VIN, SW, FB, EN and GND; the VOUT test point paired with a dedicated scope-ground pad at \textasciitilde{}5 mm spacing so a scope spring ground reaches both (this satisfies the brief's "low-inductance scope ground point near the output"). No THT loop test points - they add inductance and height and cost a hand-solder step. 14. \textbf{Is EN to be user-controllable (jumper/header), or purely an internal UVLO node?} Default: internal only - a resistor divider from VIN sets UVLO at approximately 6.5 V rising / 6.0 V falling, so the converter refuses to start below the 7 V spec floor, and EN is exposed as a test pad only. 15. \textbf{Minimum operating ambient?} Default: 0 C operating, with all parts rated -40 C or lower so the limit is the specification and not the silicon. 16. \textbf{Enclosure: is the 50 C figure free-air ambient or inside a sealed box?} Default: open-frame, free-air 50 C, mounted on standoffs with unobstructed convection on both faces. If it is ever boxed, the internal air temperature must be re-stated - a sealed enclosure would likely break the thermal budget. 17. \textbf{May the board use the full 50 x 40 mm, or should it be as small as possible?} Default: use the full 50 x 40 mm envelope. Copper area is the free variable that closes the thermal case, and the brief caps the size rather than asking for minimum size. 18. \textbf{2-layer or 4-layer?} Default: 4-layer. The brief's own layout section demands "an uninterrupted ground plane on the layer directly under the switching components", a single low-impedance ground reference, and enough copper to sink \textasciitilde{}2 W by convection - all three are materially easier and lower-risk on 4 layers, and the JLCPCB cost delta at prototype quantity is small. Justification to be recorded at P5. 19. \textbf{Mounting hole geometry.} Default: 3.2 mm holes, non-plated (NPTH), one at each corner inset 3.5 mm from both edges, 6.5 mm diameter copper/mask keepout for an M3 washer, isolated from GND (no chassis-ground bond, avoiding an uncontrolled ground loop through the standoffs). 20. \textbf{Maximum component height?} Default: 15 mm above the top surface, which comfortably fits a 5.08 mm screw terminal (\textasciitilde{}10 mm) and any shielded power inductor likely to be chosen (\textless{}7 mm). 21. \textbf{Copper weight?} Default: JLCPCB standard stackup - 1 oz (35 um) outer, 0.5 oz inner on 4-layer (the brief explicitly warns to check this). Escalate to 2 oz outer only if the IPC-2152 sizing or the junction-temperature calculation fails at 1 oz; record the escalation if it happens. 22. \textbf{Build quantity?} Default: 5 boards (JLCPCB prototype minimum). 23. \textbf{Target unit cost?} Default: no hard cap; keep the BOM under roughly \$12/board at qty 5 and flag any single line item over \textasciitilde{}\$3 for a conscious decision. 24. \textbf{LCSC stock threshold to call a part "available"?} Default: \textgreater{}= 500 pcs in stock for the buck IC, inductor and P-FET; \textgreater{}= 2000 pcs for passives; and no part whose LCSC page shows an end-of-life or "last stock" state. 25. \textbf{Assembly method, including the two THT screw terminals?} Default: JLCPCB PCBA for all SMT parts; the two screw terminals hand-soldered on receipt (avoids JLC's THT surcharge on a 5-board run and keeps the connector choice free of JLC's THT part list). Both connector footprints must still be documented in the BOM/CPL as DNP-for-assembly. 26. \textbf{Single- or double-sided assembly?} Default: single-sided, top only. All active and passive parts on top; bottom reserved for ground plane, thermal copper and the test pads' ground stitching. This halves assembly cost and keeps the bottom face free to conduct heat. 27. \textbf{JLCPCB process class?} Default: the standard/economic class (typically 5 mil (0.127 mm) minimum trace and space, 0.3 mm minimum drill, 0.13 mm annular ring). Nothing in this design needs finer, and staying standard keeps cost and yield where they should be. Actual limits to be confirmed against JLC's published capability table at P5, not from memory. 28. \textbf{LCSC Basic vs Extended parts?} Default: prefer Basic/Preferred for R, C, L and the LED; accept Extended for the buck IC, the power inductor and the P-channel FET where the requirement demands a specific part. Extended parts add a per-line feeder fee - acceptable at these quantities. 29. \textbf{Required behaviour under a sustained output short circuit?} Default: the board must survive indefinitely and recover automatically when the short is removed (hiccup-mode current limit), without exceeding component ratings and without the input fuse blowing unless a genuine hard failure has occurred. 30. {*}{*}Required behaviour if the OUTPUT terminal is back-driven, or if input and output connectors are swapped by the user (they are identical 2-pin 5.08 mm parts)?{*}{*} Default: no active output reverse-current or back-drive protection is required, but the silkscreen must unambiguously mark IN/OUT and polarity on both connectors, and the board should not be destroyed by a brief 5 V back-feed into the output. A swapped connection driving 12 V into the 5 V output is NOT required to be survivable - it will be prevented by labelling. Flag if survivability is actually wanted. 31. \textbf{Any EMI standard to meet (CISPR 32 / EN 55032 class B conducted or radiated)?} Default: no formal standard and no compliance testing; apply the brief's layout rules as best practice, leave the DNP snubber footprint as the mitigation hook, and add no input EMI filter beyond the bulk plus ceramic input capacitance already required. 32. \textbf{Switching frequency preference?} Default: no hard requirement - choose whatever the selected IC family supports in the roughly 400-800 kHz range, trading inductor size against switching loss and the \textgreater{}88\% efficiency floor. If a specific band must be avoided (e.g. AM broadcast, 530-1710 kHz), say so, since that would rule out several otherwise-suitable 1 MHz-class parts. Note the requirement interacts with Q31. 33. \textbf{Silkscreen content?} Default: board name "sbuck-5v3a", revision "A", date, input and output voltage/current markings at each terminal, polarity (+/-) on both connectors, pin-1/polarity marks on every polarised part, and every test point labelled. No logo.

\subsection*{Sheet plan}
\subsection*{sbuck-5v3a - schematic sheet plan, net contract and refdes map}
\subsubsection*{1. Sheet plan: ONE flat root sheet}
\begin{quote}\small\ttfamily\raggedright
\textbar{} Sheet \textbar{} Blocks (`blocks.md`) \textbar{} Refdes block \textbar{} `\#PWR` base \textbar{}\\
\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}\\
\textbar{} {*}{*}root{*}{*} (no child sheets) \textbar{} B1-B9, all of them \textbar{} {*}{*}1-99{*}{*} \textbar{} {*}{*}100{*}{*} \textbar{}
\end{quote}
\textbf{Decided: a single root sheet, no hierarchy.} 33 placed parts (2 of them DNP) plus 7 test pads and 4 mounting holes. This is one function - a single-rail converter - with one floorplan that runs straight through from the left edge to the right edge, so there is no organising principle for a split to express. The full-run recipe explicitly allows one schematic agent for a board this size.

The decisive argument is the \textbf{net-naming risk}, not the part count. KiCad names a net from a hierarchical label as \texttt{/\textless{}sheet\textgreater{}/\textless{}LABEL\textgreater{}}, and every \texttt{constraints.json} consumer at P5-P8 matches on the exact string; a mismatch is silently no-op'd rather than failing. That trap cost the lumina-par run a P4 amendment and forced rf-de-20m into a binding root-label contract for a single crossing net. A flat sheet removes the entire class: local labels come out as \texttt{/NAME} and power symbols come out bare, with no sheet prefix anywhere.

Refdes are unique by construction on one sheet. The blocks below are a \emph{readability} convention for the BOM, not a uniqueness mechanism.

---

\subsubsection*{2. Net-naming contract - BINDING ON P4}
These are the CANONICAL names. \texttt{constraints.json} matches them literally.

\begin{quote}\small\ttfamily\raggedright
\textbar{} Canonical net \textbar{} Kind \textbar{} Carries \textbar{}\\
\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}\\
\textbar{} `/VIN` \textbar{} local label \textbar{} J1.1 -\textgreater{} F1 -\textgreater{} Q1 drain. {*}{*}2.44 A at 7 V{*}{*}, raw and unprotected \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} `+VIN` \textbar{} {*}{*}power symbol / global label (bare){*}{*} \textbar{} Q1 source -\textgreater{} C4-C9 -\textgreater{} U1 VIN. 2.6 A design, 1.5 A rms in the ceramics \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} `/SW` \textbar{} local label \textbar{} U1 SW -\textgreater{} L1. {*}{*}3.53 A pk, hard-switched, 500 kHz{*}{*} \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} `+5V` \textbar{} {*}{*}power symbol / global label (bare){*}{*} \textbar{} L1 -\textgreater{} C10-C15 -\textgreater{} J2. 3.3 A design ceiling \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} `GND` \textbar{} {*}{*}power symbol (bare){*}{*} \textbar{} F.Cu island + In1 + In2 + B.Cu. 3.3 A return \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} `/EN` \textbar{} local label \textbar{} R2/R3 junction -\textgreater{} U1 EN. TP5 \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} `/FB` \textbar{} local label \textbar{} R6/R7 junction -\textgreater{} U1 FB. High-Z, keep away from `/SW` and L1 \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} `/COMP` \textbar{} local label \textbar{} U1 COMP -\textgreater{} R5 -\textgreater{} C2 -\textgreater{} GND \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} `/BST` \textbar{} local label \textbar{} C1 -\textgreater{} U1 BST \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} `/RT` \textbar{} local label \textbar{} U1 RT -\textgreater{} R4 -\textgreater{} GND \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} `/QGATE` \textbar{} local label \textbar{} Q1 gate, R1 to GND, D2 anode \textbar{}
\end{quote}
\textbf{Rules P4 must not break:}

1. \texttt{+VIN}, \texttt{+5V} and \texttt{GND} must be \textbf{power symbols or global labels} so they come out bare. A local label would produce \texttt{/+VIN} and five \texttt{constraints.json} entries would stop matching in silence. 2. Every other net above must be a \textbf{local label on the root sheet}, producing the leading \texttt{/}. Do not "tidy" the slash away. 3. {*}{*}Do not rename anything to end in \texttt{\_P}, \texttt{\_N}, \texttt{\_H}, \texttt{\_L}, \texttt{DP}, \texttt{DM}, \texttt{+} or \texttt{-}.{*}{*} \texttt{rules\_gen.detect\_diff\_pairs} auto-pairs \texttt{high\_speed} nets with those suffixes; \texttt{/SW} is declared under \texttt{high\_speed} and a suffix collision would silently emit differential-pair gap rules and an inner-layer track ban on the most current-carrying node on the board. Current names are safe. 4. \texttt{diff\_pairs} is an \textbf{explicit empty list} in \texttt{constraints.json} - there is no differential net on this board and the empty list disables auto-discovery.

\subsubsection*{4. Floorplan for P6 - straight-through, left to right}
The board is 50 mm wide (x) by 40 mm tall (y); the {*}{*}short edges are left and right{*}{*}, which is where the two connectors go (Q10).

\begin{quote}\small\ttfamily\raggedright
\textbar{} Zone \textbar{} x \textbar{} Contents \textbar{}\\
\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}\\
\textbar{} {*}{*}input{*}{*} \textbar{} 0 - 13 \textbar{} J1, F1, Q1, D2, R1, C4. The coolest corner - C4's life is set by local board temperature \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} {*}{*}converter{*}{*} \textbar{} 13 - 32 \textbar{} C5-C9, U1 (thermal island, centred near x=21 y=20), C1, R2-R5, C2, C3, /SW pour, R9/C16, L1 \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} {*}{*}output{*}{*} \textbar{} 32 - 50 \textbar{} C10-C15, R6/R7, D1/R8, TP1-TP7, J2 \textbar{}
\end{quote}
Non-negotiables that no annealer can discover:

1. \textbf{Hot loop first.} \texttt{C5-C9 -\textgreater{} U1 VIN -\textgreater{} U1 PGND -\textgreater{} C5-C9} is the shortest loop on the board, all on F.Cu, with C9 physically closest to the pin and In1 solid GND directly beneath as the image plane. 2. \textbf{`/SW` is a short wide pour}: \textgreater{}= 2.5 mm wide, \textless{}= 8 mm long, \textless{}= 40 mm\textasciicircum{}2, F.Cu only, never inner, never near a board edge or connector. The TP2 tap is a stub that counts against the 40 mm\textasciicircum{}2. 3. \textbf{R6/R7 and the `/FB` trace hug the FB pin and stay away from `/SW` and L1} - an explicit rule in all three candidate vendor layouts. 4. \textbf{R9/C16 sit directly across the SW pour to PGND} with a low-inductance path even while unpopulated. Place by explicit \texttt{place\_edit}. 5. \textbf{C4 and F1 stay \textgreater{}= 10-12 mm from U1 and L1} (declared as \texttt{separation} entries): C4 because its life halves every 10 C, F1 because it is a deliberate 0.15 W heat source. 6. \textbf{16 thermal vias in U1's pad} at 0.3 mm / 1.0 mm pitch, plus 8-12 stitching vias in the surrounding F.Cu island. \texttt{check\_thermal} will not catch their absence (see \texttt{power\_tree.md} s4.3) - this is a review gate. 7. \textbf{No layer transitions on `/VIN`, `+VIN`, `/SW` or `+5V`.} A transition needs 6-8 vias at 0.5 A/via. GND is plane-fed through the stitching field.

Parts to place by explicit \texttt{place\_edit} and \textbf{lock} before the annealer runs: \texttt{U1}, \texttt{L1}, \texttt{C5-C9}, \texttt{C1}, \texttt{R9}, \texttt{C16}, \texttt{J1}, \texttt{J2}, \texttt{H1-H4}.

\subsubsection*{5. P4 notes (schematic phase)}
1. \textbf{Re-derive the compensation.} The vendor's Rcomp/Ccomp are quoted for 2x 22 uF; the bank is 5x 22 uF. Target fc 25-50 kHz, phase margin \textgreater{}= 45 deg, using the AP64350 datasheet's Eqs 12-20. Record the numbers on the schematic. If the loop cannot close there, drop to 4x 22 uF and record it. 2. \textbf{R6/R7 must be 0.1\% parts in the BOM}, not 1\% with a 0.1\% note. The reference tolerance alone spends 60\% of the +/-2\% window. 3. \textbf{UVLO is 6.2 V / 5.3 V, not the delegate's 6.5 / 6.0.} Use the AP64350 divider equations (they include the 4.114 uA and 5.5 uA internal pull-ups - a naive divider calculation is wrong) and verify against the P8 sim bench. 4. \textbf{No gate RC on Q1 and no gate capacitor.} The body diode already bypasses the channel during inrush. This is a decision, not an omission - do not let ERC or a reviewer add one. 5. \textbf{The snubber R9/C16 must exist in the netlist} as DNP so their pads, clearance and routing are accounted for at P6/P7. Populating later is then a BOM change, not a respin. 6. \textbf{Test pads are real nets.} TP7 is a second GND pad placed for a scope spring ground, \textasciitilde{}5 mm from TP3, not a duplicate of TP6. 7. \textbf{Silkscreen} (Q33): board name + rev A + date; "VIN 7-18V" and "VOUT 5V 3A" with polarity marks at both terminals - this is the \emph{only} mitigation for a swapped-connector event, which is not survivable by design; pin-1 marks on every polarised part; every test point labelled; no logo. 8. \textbf{J1 and J2 are DNP for assembly} and must appear as such in the BOM/CPL.

Two warnings were FIXED rather than waived (see below). Five are waived here.

\subsubsection*{FIXED, not waived}
\textbf{F1. DNP snubber overstressed its own resistor.} C\emph{V\textasciicircum{}2}fsw = 162 mW at 18 V and 338 mW at the declared 26 V ring, into an 0603 rated 0.1 W. A DNP footprint that destroys itself when populated is a trap, not a feature. Fixed: R9 0603 -\textgreater{} 1206 (\textgreater{}= 0.25 W), C16 1 nF X7R -\textgreater{} 470 pF C0G 1206. New figures 76 mW at 18 V, 159 mW at 26 V. Both values stay inside the documented 10-33 ohm / 470 pF-2.2 nF bring-up range from blocks.md B9.

\textbf{F2. Loop calibration claim withdrawn.} P4 claimed its model was validated against the vendor Bode plot ("PM 79-84 deg vs published 81.6"). The reviewer read Fig.29 and found the plotted circuit HAS C4 = 33 pF fitted, so the comparison used the wrong model variant. The x0.83 realisation factor is therefore unevidenced. The claim is withdrawn from the record; the design is re-stated on its worst reading.

---

\subsubsection*{WAIVED}
\textbf{W1. Loop phase margin is less certain than P4 claimed.} Reviewer's independent re-derivation reproduces P4's fc/PM/\textbar{}T\textbar{} table to the digit, so the arithmetic is right; what fails is the calibration against the vendor plot. Worst-case reading gives PM \textasciitilde{}46-53 deg against the \textgreater{}= 45 deg requirement. \emph{Waived because}: it still meets requirement on every reading, and the vendor's own published GM (-26.8 dB) matches neither model variant (-8.3 with feedforward, -18.4 without), i.e. the vendor's "first-order calculated" model carries HF poles that no reader-built model reproduces. Closing this needs a real loop measurement or the vendor's own model - not more reading. \textbf{Carried to P8 as a bench item.}

\textbf{W2. Load step: 148 mV modelled, 200 mV on the corrected reading - AT the limit.} SUPERSEDED TWICE, and the honest number got worse each time. The first restatement (181 mV) still carried the withdrawn 0.83 factor. Re-running the vendor comparison like-for-like - model WITH C4=33pF and C6=47pF fitted, matching the circuit actually plotted in Fig.29 - gives a factor of 0.743, not 0.83, and the model is optimistic on all three axes (fc +35\%, PM +19.4 deg, GM +18.5 dB). Applying those offsets: \textbf{dV = 200 mV against a 200 mV limit.} Additionally the 0-\textgreater{}3 A step STARTS IN PFM (automatic PWM/PFM, no MODE pin) which the CCM model does not describe.

\emph{Waived - as an at-limit DISCLOSURE, not a pass} - because: 1. \textbf{No R5 value clears all three targets.} Measured sweep, recorded in root.py s2.5a so the "just raise R5" reflex is answered in the source: 75k -\textgreater{} PM 45.6 deg / dV 200 mV; 82k -\textgreater{} PM 44.1 deg FAIL / dV 183 mV; 91k -\textgreater{} PM 39.9 deg FAIL / dV 165 mV. Raising fc buys sampling-pole lag. 75k is the only value that keeps phase margin - the binding requirement - above its floor. 2. \textbf{Adding output capacitance does not help.} fc scales as 1/COUT at fixed compensation, so fc\emph{COUT is constant and dV = dI/(2}pi\emph{fc}COUT) is INVARIANT in COUT. Buying more caps would be pure cost for zero transient improvement. 3. \textbf{It is not a measurement.} It extrapolates a one-point vendor calibration, taken at a different operating point, onto a different circuit. It is a plausibility band, not a second reading. 4. \textbf{The dominant uncertainty is larger than the shortfall.} The COUT derating band is +/-13\% around its mean with no vendor DC-bias curve behind it. 5. \textbf{Re-tunable without a respin}: R5, C2 and C3 are three adjacent 0603 parts.

\textbf{Carried to P8 and to bring-up as the board's \#1 bench item.}

{*}{*}W2b. P8 UPDATE - the phase-margin floor is NOT actually bounded, and this disclosure must stop reading as "0.6 deg clear".{*}{*} The P8 fresh-context review accepted the dV COUT-invariance argument but found the PM argument incomplete: PM is NOT invariant in COUT, and the {[}75.0, 96.8{]} uF band is \textbf{DC-bias-only}. Hot X7R derating and aging are named in root.py as pushing toward the low end but were never STACKED. Stacked, the effective bank is \textasciitilde{}62.7 uF - about 20\% below the swept corner - which on the sweep's own slope costs \textasciitilde{}3 deg and puts {*}{*}PM at roughly 42-44 deg, under the 45 deg floor{*}{*}. No respin is implied (R5/C2/C3 are three 0603 parts and this is already bring-up bench item \#1), but the honest statement is that the loop margin at the true COUT floor is UNBOUNDED BY ANALYSIS, not comfortably clear. Closing it needs a network analyser, not more modelling.

\textbf{W2a. The fc floor of 24.4 kHz is NOT a requirement miss.} The "fc 25-50 kHz" target was the ORCHESTRATOR's proxy, written into the P4 spawn prompt as a stand-in for the real requirement, which is "recovery within 100 us". At fc = 24.4 kHz settling is 5/(2\emph{pi}fc) = \textbf{32.6 us, a 3.1x margin on the 100 us spec}. The proxy was simply stricter than the requirement it stood for. Recorded so that no later phase re-litigates a 2.4\% miss against a number that was never the spec.

\textbf{W3. Hot-plug inrush peak cannot be bounded from published data.} The 57 A figure comes from the 0.30 ohm path row; the 26 V node rating comes from the 0.05 ohm row of the same table, which assumes an ALL-CERAMIC Cin. At 0.10 ohm the formula gives 180 A against Q1's -60 A channel IDM. \emph{Waived because}: this board deliberately does NOT have an all-ceramic Cin - C4 carries 80 mOhm ESR as a stated DAMPING requirement - so the 0.05 ohm row is not this configuration. The 26 V declaration is kept anyway as conservative headroom for part ratings. Residual and honest: AO4407A's body-diode single-pulse capability is not published, and screw terminals are a wire-then-power connector, not a hot-plug one. \textbf{Recorded in DECISIONS.md as an accepted, quantified risk.}

\textbf{W4. Q1 gate dv/dt immunity is unbounded.} parts/C16072.json publishes Qg and Rg but no Ciss/Crss/Coss for the AO4407A. \emph{Waived because}: the datum does not exist in the sourced datasheet, so no analysis can close it. Stated as a limit of knowledge rather than assumed benign.

{*}{*}W5. UVLO effective anti-motorboating margin is 0.32 V, not the 0.41 V argued at P2{*}{*} (the fuse and FET drops were omitted from that argument). \emph{Waived because}: the margin is still POSITIVE, and the raw hysteresis (0.905 V, VON 6.230 / VOFF 5.325, verified exactly against the vendor's pull-up-inclusive Eq.2/3) comfortably exceeds the 0.49 V cable drop that motivated the P2 override. Worst-case VON 6.67 V sits 0.33 V below the 7.0 V minimum input, so the converter starts across its whole rated range.

\subsection*{Design review of record}
\subsection*{P8 board review - sbuck-5v3a (fresh context, adversarial)}
Reviewer did not place, route or fix this board. Every geometric number below was re-measured from \texttt{kicad/sbuck-5v3a.kicad\_pcb} with pcbnew + shapely, not read from a prior phase's report. Renders regenerated at 2400 px: \texttt{reports/renders/sbuck-5v3a\_\{top,bottom,iso\}.png}.

{*}{*}Gate: 2 errors, 12 warnings. Both existing waiver groups upheld (9 findings), one with a corrected justification. Two new items recommended for documented-deviation status (W1 \texttt{/SW} length, W12 mounting-hole keepout).{*}{*}

Independent re-runs (my own, not inherited):

\begin{itemize}
\item \texttt{verify\_all} reproduces the gate exactly: 28 total, 9 error (all waived), 19 warning.
Nothing was SKIPPED for missing inputs.
\item \texttt{kc.py drc --parity --all-track-errors}: \textbf{0 violations, 0 unconnected}. Confirmed.
\item \texttt{check\_irdrop} / \texttt{check\_pdn\_z} / \texttt{check\_thermal} re-read; arithmetic re-derived below.
\end{itemize}
---

\subsubsection*{ERRORS}
\paragraph*{E1. D2's cathode marker \texttt{K} is printed at the anode end - \texttt{F.SilkS}, \texttt{(41.720, 59.125)}}
The board-level \texttt{gr\_text "K"} added at P6 sits at x 41.72. D2 is at (43.620, 60.825) rot 180:

\begin{quote}\small\ttfamily\raggedright
\textbar{} \textbar{} board x \textbar{} net \textbar{} role \textbar{}\\
\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}\\
\textbar{} pad 1 \textbar{} 45.26 \textbar{} `+VIN` \textbar{} {*}{*}cathode{*}{*} \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} pad 2 \textbar{} 41.98 \textbar{} `/QGATE` \textbar{} anode \textbar{}
\end{quote}
Evidence the cathode is pad 1, three ways: the symbol (\texttt{lib/aiee.kicad\_sym}, BZT52C15) declares pin 1 name \texttt{K}, pin 2 name \texttt{A}; the footprint (\texttt{lib/aiee.pretty/SOD-123\_L2.7-W1.6-LS3.7-RD.kicad\_mod}) draws its band at local x -0.97 and its pin-1 dot at local (-1.85, 0.80), \textbf{both on the pad-1 side}; and the netlist puts pad 1 on \texttt{+VIN}, which is where the cathode of a Vgs clamp belongs.

The \texttt{K} text is 0.26 mm from pad 2's x-span (it sits directly above the anode pad) and 3.54 mm from the cathode. \textbf{It contradicts the same part's own band and dot.} Two conflicting cathode indications is worse than none.

Consequence, if a board is hand-built or reworked to the silk: D2 goes in backwards and becomes a plain forward diode from \texttt{+VIN} to \texttt{/QGATE}, holding Vgs at about -0.7 V. AO4407A's Vgs(th) is -1 to -3 V, so Q1 never enhances and the whole 2.6 A input current runs in its body diode - roughly 0.8 V x 2.6 A = \textbf{2.1 W in an SO-8 with no heatsinking}. Q1 dies and the reverse-polarity protection goes with it.

The circuit is correct; only the marker is wrong. Fix: \texttt{silk\_place} the text to \textasciitilde{}(45.6, 59.1), or delete it and let the footprint band do the job. \textbf{domain: silk.}

Cross-check that this is an isolated slip, not a systematic one: D1's \texttt{K} at (64.770, 71.625) IS correct - \texttt{LED0805-R-RD} puts pad 1 at local +1.05 (anode, net \texttt{/LEDA}) and pad 2 at -1.05 with the chamfered cathode bracket, and the marker is at pad 2. Only D2 is wrong.

\paragraph*{E2. Eight refdes labels are attributed to the wrong part - \texttt{F.SilkS}}
These are \texttt{check\_silk}'s eight \texttt{silk\_misattributed} \textbf{warnings}. They were neither fixed nor waived - they simply fell through the P8 gate, which only fails on \texttt{error}. They are real, and three of them are worse than "misattributed":

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{`R5` / `C2` / `R3` print as a left-to-right row above the parts C2 / R5 / C3}
(x 40.22 / 43.22 / 46.22, all at y 55.025). Every label in that row names a different
part from the one beneath it. \texttt{C2}'s text at (44.995, 53.025) is 0.47 mm from C3;
\texttt{R3}'s at (46.72, 53.318) is 0.27 mm from R6 and 1.7 mm above C3, while the real R3 is
4.6 mm away at (44.720, 57.425). Values involved: C2 = 3.3 nF, R5 = 75 k, C3 = 10 pF,
R3 = 24.0 k - four different parts, three swappable 0603 bodies. Visible directly on
\texttt{reports/renders/sbuck-5v3a\_top.png}.
\item \textbf{`C9` at (35.695, 48.060) prints ON C7} (0.00 mm). C9 is the 100 nF 0603 that sets the
hot loop; C7 is a 4.7 uF 1206.
\item \textbf{`R7` at (53.298, 55.725) prints ON C12.}
\end{itemize}
Plus \texttt{Q1}-\textgreater{}C4 (0.65 mm), \texttt{TP1}-\textgreater{}F1 (0.29 mm), \texttt{TP2}-\textgreater{}R9 (0.25 mm), \texttt{TP7}-\textgreater{}TP6 (0.70 mm).

Why this is an error and not cosmetics on this board specifically: \texttt{parts/parts.json} records J1/J2 as \textbf{DNP for JLC assembly, hand-soldered on receipt}, so a human is building part of this board from the silk; and TP1/TP2/TP7 mislabel probe points on a live 18 V converter.

The \textbf{functional} test-point legends are fine and correctly placed - \texttt{+VIN}, \texttt{SW}, \texttt{EN}, \texttt{GND}, \texttt{GND-S}, \texttt{FB}, \texttt{+5V} each sit adjacent to their own pad (verified on the render). This finding is about the refdes layer only.

Scripted fix, no copper touched: \texttt{place\_edit.py move\_text} / \texttt{silk\_place.py}. \textbf{domain: silk.}

\subsubsection*{WAIVER AUDIT - the nine waived findings}
\paragraph*{Waiver group 1: 7 x \texttt{check\_silk} "silk circle covers pad TPn.1 (1.77 mm2)" - \textbf{UPHELD}}
Verified on three independent legs. The first two are decisive; the third I had to prove rather than accept.

\textbf{(a) The geometry, read straight out of the board file.} All seven TPs carry:

\begin{quote}\small\ttfamily\raggedright
(fp\_circle (center 0 0) (end 0 0.95) (stroke (width 0.12) (type solid)) (fill no) (layer "F.SilkS"))\\
(pad "1" smd circle (at 0 0) (size 1.5 1.5) (layers "F.Cu" "F.Mask"))
\end{quote}
pcbnew reports \texttt{GetFillMode() = 1}, and \texttt{pcbnew.FILL\_T\_NO\_FILL == 1} (KiCad's enum starts at 1; \texttt{FILLED\_SHAPE == 2}). Ring inner edge = 0.95 - 0.12/2 = \textbf{0.89 mm}; pad radius = \textbf{0.75 mm}; clearance \textbf{0.14 mm}. The claim is exactly right.

\textbf{(b) The checker bug, located.} \texttt{check\_silk.py:167-172}:

\begin{quote}\small\ttfamily\raggedright
if kind.endswith("circle"):\\
    c, e = \_nums(\_kid(node, "center")), \_nums(\_kid(node, "end"))\\
    r = math.hypot(e{[}0{]} - c{[}0{]}, e{[}1{]} - c{[}1{]})\\
    return Point(xf((c{[}0{]}, c{[}1{]}))).buffer(r + w2)      \# \textless{}- FILLED disc
\end{quote}
\texttt{\_shape\_geom} never reads the \texttt{(fill ...)} node at all, for any shape kind. So the ring becomes a filled disc of radius 0.95 + 0.06 = 1.01 mm, which swallows the pad whole. Reported overlap 1.7659 mm2 vs pi{*}0.75\textasciicircum{}2 = 1.76715 - a 0.07\% shortfall that is just shapely's polygon approximation of a circle. Exactly the signature the waiver claims.

\textbf{(c) The DRC cross-check is valid here, but its stated generality is not.} I did not take "kicad-cli DRC reports 0 violations" on trust. On a scratch copy I shrank TP4's silk ring to r = 0.30 - \textbf{entirely inside} the 0.75 mm pad - and `kicad-cli pcb drc --severity-all` still reported \textbf{0 violations}. I then injected two fat silk segments \textbf{crossing} TP3, U1.2, U1.9 and C9's pads and got 5 x \texttt{silk\_over\_copper} + 9 x \texttt{silk\_overlap} warnings. So:

\textgreater{} KiCad's \texttt{silk\_over\_copper} fires on silk that crosses a pad's mask aperture, and stays \textgreater{} silent on silk fully enclosed inside one.

A ring at r = 0.95 overlapping a 0.75 mm pad would be a \emph{crossing}, so DRC's silence on this board \textbf{is} real evidence and leg (c) stands. But the waiver's wider phrasing - "the playbook itself directs that silk be verified with \texttt{kc.py drc} rather than \texttt{check\_silk}" - is too broad and should be narrowed in the record: \texttt{kc.py drc} is not a general substitute for \texttt{check\_silk}, and this board has no working automated check for enclosed-silk cases.

\textbf{Verdict: waiving the checker, not the geometry. Correct. Keep all seven.}

\paragraph*{Waiver group 2: 2 x \texttt{check\_pdn} "+5V / GND has no decoupling capacitors" - \textbf{UPHELD, but the stated reason is wrong in a way that matters}}
The \textbf{call} is right. The \textbf{reason} is not, and the difference changes what the human should be told.

\texttt{check\_pdn} does not model "a supply rail must have decoupling capacitors near its IC pins". Reading the source: \texttt{rail\_caps()} filters \texttt{decoupling.json{[}"associations"{]}} by \texttt{rail == \textless{}net\textgreater{}} and raises an error if that list is empty. \textbf{It never looks at the board.} Near-pin geometry is \texttt{check\_decoupling}'s job, and that check passed on its five \texttt{+VIN} associations (loop 5.05-11.50 nH).

So the finding is not a category error about IC pins. It is a literal and true statement about the project's own metadata: {*}{*}no \texttt{decoupling.json} association names \texttt{+5V}, so no automated check has ever looked at the output bank.{*}{*} "Nothing is hidden" overstates it.

What I verified about the rails themselves, so the human knows the substance is sound:

\begin{itemize}
\item The \texttt{+5V} bank exists and is connected: C10-C14 (5 x 22 uF 1210) and C15 (4.7 uF 0805)
all carry a \texttt{+5V} pad and a \texttt{GND} partner; \texttt{+5V} F.Cu is \textbf{one 198.93 mm2 island};
\texttt{kc.py drc --parity} is clean, so schematic and board agree.
\item \texttt{check\_irdrop} DID run on both nets with the real geometry (they were correctly NOT
given \texttt{pdn:false}): \texttt{+5V} worst drop \textbf{8.96 mV}, \texttt{GND} \textbf{1.15 mV}, against a
+/-100 mV output window. This is the leg that actually covers these two rails.
\item \texttt{GND} is a return net; decoupling to itself is meaningless. Correct.
\end{itemize}
{*}{*}Verdict: keep both waivers, but restate the reason as "check\_pdn is a metadata inventory and \texttt{+5V} has no association declared; coverage for this rail comes from check\_irdrop and P4 arithmetic, not from a PDN check". Also fix \texttt{decoupling.json}'s \texttt{\_note}, which still claims \texttt{+5V} is handled by \texttt{pdn=false} - \texttt{constraints.json} records that as reverted.{*}{*}

\paragraph*{Was deleting 3 of the 9 ring vias right?}
Yes, on the evidence. The ring vias sit 1.12-1.17 mm outside the EP edges and serve secondary spreading; the 12-via EP array is the primary junction-to-plane path and is untouched. The stated reason (they sat in 1.06-1.58 mm GND fingers) is the right kind of reason, because a 0.6 mm via in a 1.06 mm finger leaves 0.23 mm each side. And the check that would catch the consequence is armed: \texttt{GND} is declared \texttt{plane\_fed: true}, which keeps \textbf{pour-neck findings at ERROR severity at the full 3.3 A budget}, and \texttt{check\_current} reports \textbf{zero} pour-neck errors - only the ten leaf-tap advisories. Thermal cost of 9 -\textgreater{} 6 in the ring is second-order against the EP array.

\paragraph*{The mounting-hole keepout that was never built}
\texttt{constraints.json} placement note (3) asked for a 6.5 mm mask/copper keepout at each M3 hole, hand-added as rule areas after the pours. \textbf{There are no rule areas on this board.} I checked the consequence rather than assuming it: all four layers are GND at every hole (In1/In2/B.Cu each void a 3.7 mm circle around the 3.2 mm NPTH, so no inner copper is exposed at the barrel), and the nearest \textbf{non-GND} copper to any hole is \textbf{5.38 mm} (H2, F.Cu) against an M3 washer radius of 3.25 mm - \textbf{2.13 mm clear}. Benign. Record it as a knowingly-dropped constraint rather than leaving it silently unmet.

\subsubsection*{U1's THERMAL NUMBER - which model to believe}
{*}{*}Do not report "54.17 C against 55 allowed, 0.83 C of headroom" as this board's tightest number. It is not a measurement of this board at all.{*}{*}

\texttt{check\_thermal} computes `a\_eff = min(A\_SAT = 645, sum over layers of heatsink-net copper within 14.3 mm)\texttt{. I measured that sum: {*}{*}2137.56 mm2{*}{*}. So }a\_eff` \textbf{clamps} to 645, and

\begin{quote}\small\ttfamily\raggedright
theta = 45 + 95 {*} exp(-645/235) = 45 + 95{*}0.06427 = 51.1055 C/W\\
rise  = 1.06 {*} 51.1055 = 54.17 C
\end{quote}
At the clamp, \texttt{theta} is a \textbf{universal constant} for any 4-layer board with \textgreater{}= 645 mm2 of heatsink copper. The 12 thermal vias, the three 1850 mm2 planes, U1's position near board centre - every one of them moves this result by exactly \textbf{0.00 C}. What "54.17 vs 55" measures is the distance between two \emph{declared inputs}: \texttt{power\_w = 1.06} and \texttt{dt\_c = 55}.

\texttt{check\_thermal} is also \textbf{not additive}: U1's 54.17 C and L1's 42.51 C are each computed as if that part were the only heat source on the board. They cannot both be "the rise".

\textbf{Believe the P1/P2 board-level ladder.} I re-derived its inputs from scratch before looking at its answer:

\begin{quote}\small\ttfamily\raggedright
h\_conv = 1.42{*}(dT/L)\textasciicircum{}0.25 = 1.42{*}(37/0.05)\textasciicircum{}0.25            = 7.41 W/m2K\\
h\_rad  = 0.9{*}sigma{*}(358\textasciicircum{}2+323\textasciicircum{}2){*}(358+323)                 = 8.08 W/m2K   (they used 8.2)\\
h\_tot  = 15.5 W/m2K over A\_eff 3.4e-3 m2  -\textgreater{}  R\_ba         = 19.0 C/W
\end{quote}
That reproduces their \texttt{R\_ba = 19 C/W} to about 2\%, from textbook flat-plate correlations, and the ladder \texttt{Tj = Ta + P\_board{*}R\_ba + dT\_local + P\_IC{*}(theta\_JC,bot + R\_via)} is the correct physics for a near-isothermal board (spreading length 32 mm \textgreater{} the 20-25 mm board half-dimension). Worst \textbf{Tj = 97.9 C at 7 V}.

Two corrections to that ladder that nobody has applied:

1. \textbf{It still carries the 16-via array at 2.16 K/W.} The board has 12. \texttt{R\_1via = 29.4 K/W} -\textgreater{} 12 in parallel at the same 0.85 crowding factor is \textasciitilde{}2.88 K/W, so \texttt{+1.058 {*} (2.88 - 2.16) = +0.76 C}. \textbf{Worst Tj \textasciitilde{}= 98.7 C, margin 6.3 C, not 7.1 C.} The P2 digest table was not updated for the P6 16 -\textgreater{} 12 change. 2. \textbf{The honest band.} \texttt{R\_ba} is stated at +/-30\%, and only the \texttt{P\_board{*}R\_ba} term scales: \texttt{50 + 34.7{*}0.7 + 6 + 7.2 = 87.5 C} to \texttt{50 + 34.7{*}1.3 + 6 + 7.2 = 108.4 C}. The upper edge crosses the 105 C \emph{design} limit but stays {*}{*}17 C below the 125 C conservative spec floor\textbf{ and }51 C below AP64350's actual 150 C Tj max{*}{*}.

\textbf{What to say to the human.} The thermal risk on this board is dominated by {*}{*}mounting, not layout{*}{*}. 53\% of the cooling path is radiation from two faces. Boxing this board, conformal-coating it, or bolting it flat against a surface removes a large share of that and costs tens of degrees - far more than any 0.83 C. That belongs in the assembly note in bold. The layout side is already 3x over its copper criteria and cannot be improved meaningfully.

L1's 42.51 C / 45 C is conservative for the same structural reason: \texttt{a\_eff} counts only the 153.23 mm2 of \texttt{+5V} copper, excluding the 30.44 mm2 \texttt{/SW} pad and the 1838.91 mm2 of GND under the part. Counting \texttt{/SW} too gives 39.8 C. The number that matters for L1 is the board-level \texttt{T\_L1 surface 100.7-106.5 C} against the part's 155 C rating.

\textbar{} output ripple, Vin 18 V \textbar{} `1.062/(8{*}97u{*}500k)` = 2.74 mV + ESR 1.062{*}\textasciitilde{}1 mOhm = 1.1 mV -\textgreater{} {*}{*}\textasciitilde{}3.8 mV{*}{*} p-p \textbar{} 50 mV \textbar{} {*}{*}13x{*}{*} \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} setpoint \textbar{} `0.8{*}(1+105/20.0)` = {*}{*}5.0000 V{*}{*} nominal; corners with VFB 792/808 mV and 0.1\% parts = {*}{*}4.942 / 5.058 V (+/-1.16\%){*}{*} \textbar{} 4.90-5.10 V \textbar{} see below \textbar{}\\

\end{quote}
\textbf{Setpoint stack - one term is missing from the record.} \texttt{root.py} quotes the VFB tolerance and the resistor tolerance but not resistor \textbf{tempco}. ERA3AEB1053V and RT0603BRD0720KL are both +/-25 ppm/K; worst-case differential drift over the 55 K rise from 50 C to the \textasciitilde{}105 C board is \texttt{2{*}25e-6{*}55 = 0.275\%} = \textbf{14 mV}. Adding that plus load regulation and the uncompensated C12 -\textgreater{} J2 IR drop (\texttt{check\_irdrop} worst \texttt{+5V} drop 8.96 mV) to the +/-58 mV corner gives \textbf{\textasciitilde{}82 mV worst case against the 100 mV window} - still passing, with \textasciitilde{}18 mV left. Worth adding the term to the record.

\textbf{SPICE: I agree it can be skipped.} SIM-1 (the setpoint sweep) is a four-term worst-case sum, closed above in closed form. A sweep would add no information. The bench item that actually matters is the loop, and no SPICE model of this board closes that either - it needs a network analyser.

\subsubsection*{THINGS I CHECKED AND FOUND CLEAN}
\begin{itemize}
\item \texttt{kc.py drc --parity --all-track-errors}: 0 violations, 0 unconnected, schematic/PCB
parity clean. Re-run by me at P8, not inherited from P7.
\item \texttt{check\_return\_path} 0, \texttt{check\_decoupling} 0 (five \texttt{+VIN} associations, loop 5.05-11.50 nH,
C9 closest at 2.14 mm / 5.05 nH), \texttt{check\_diffpair} 0, \texttt{check\_creepage} 0.
\item \texttt{check\_irdrop}: \texttt{+VIN} 13.96 mV, \texttt{+5V} 8.96 mV, \texttt{GND} 1.15 mV. Against a +/-100 mV
output window the sense-point-to-terminal error is \textasciitilde{}0.2\%. No concern.
\item No copper on any inner layer for any non-GND net (28 vias, all GND).
\item B.Cu is a bare, uninterrupted 1850 mm2 GND face with only the four J1/J2 THT annular
rings and the vias breaking it - exactly what the radiation budget needs. Note for the
assembly doc: J1.1 (\texttt{+VIN}) and J2.1 (\texttt{+5V}) are exposed on B.Cu, so insulating
standoffs are required if the board is mounted over metal.
\item No fiducials. JLC's SMT service does not require board fiducials and the connectors are
DNP/hand-soldered, so this is a note for P9, not a finding.
\item LCSC stock present for all 24 BOM lines. {*}{*}L1 (FAUL1050-6R8MT, C5298292) at 763 pcs is
the only thin line{*}{*} - single-source, no like-for-like alternate that clears
DCR \textless{}= 25 mOhm hot at 6.8 uH. Every other line clears its floor by \textgreater{}= 4x. Schedule
risk for P9, not a board defect.
\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{OPEN - not judgeable from the artifacts}
\begin{itemize}
\item Loop phase margin at the true COUT floor (W4). Needs a network-analyser measurement;
no model available to this project closes it.
\item AO4407A dv/dt immunity - no Ciss/Crss/Coss published (already disclosed as P4 W4).
\item Whether the enclosure preserves the two radiating faces (W2). The single largest
thermal lever on this board and it lives outside the board.
\item Whether a human ever reads the silk on this board. E2's severity depends on it; I
graded it as an error because \texttt{parts.json} says J1/J2 are hand-soldered on receipt.
\end{itemize}

\#\# Findings that changed other phases\\
~\\
- {*}{*}16 thermal vias is geometrically impossible.{*}{*} EP 3.502 x 2.613 mm; four 0.55 mm\\
  lands at 1.0 mm pitch need 3.55 mm, and JLC's 0.5 mm hole-to-hole floor caps it at\\
  3x4 = 12 at 0.9-0.95 mm pitch. R\_via 2.48 vs 1.90 K/W = {*}{*}+0.5 C of Tj{*}{*}, inside\\
  the margin. `check\_thermal` would not have caught this.\\
- {*}{*}`placement.fixed` silently disabled all 8 separation constraints{*}{*} - fixed refs\\
  are excluded from the annealer's cluster list, so every pair landed in\\
  `separation\_unknown\_refs` at zero cost weight. Verified all 8 by hand; all pass.\\
- {*}{*}P5 omitted the mandatory keepout translation{*}{*} - rects were still board-local,\\
  three landed off-board, the fourth produced a phantom violation. Corrected.\\
- {*}{*}Both connector rotations in `placement.edges` were wrong{*}{*} (J1 0, J2 180 pointed\\
  both wire entries INTO the board). Correct: J1=270, J2=90. Proven by orthographic\\
  side render - the mouth is the SHORTER plastic face here, so the WRL bbox alone\\
  would have misled.\\

  polarity at both terminals, pin-1/polarity on C4/D1/D2/U1, all 7 test points\\
  labelled by signal, board name + REV A + date. This is Q30's ONLY mitigation for a\\

- {*}{*}Pour the four GND planes AND pour /SW as a zone BEFORE any autoroute.{*}{*} The 0.83\\

- 25 structural footprints are LOCKED; P8 fixers must unlock before nudging.\\
- 2 residual DRC warnings are a D2 SOD-123 footprint defect (silk clips pad 2's mask\\

Min via hole-to-hole 0.600 mm (JLC floor 0.500). `/FB` 13.34 mm total, 3.13 mm from\\
/SW copper, 3.52 mm from L1, still sensing at C12's +5V terminal. In2.Cu came out\\
{*}{*}GND{*}{*}, not +5V - checked explicitly. No placement was touched; all 25 locks intact.\\
~\\
\#\# Chain that ran\\
~\\
`planes\_gen` (7 zones) -\textgreater{} 12 in-pad thermal vias (`route\_edit`) -\textgreater{} 9 hand-placed U1\\
ring vias -\textgreater{} `stitch\_vias` (6 area vias, 15 mm auto pitch) -\textgreater{} `route\_auto`\\
(`--power-layers In1.Cu,In2.Cu,B.Cu` so every track lands on F.Cu; FR rung 1, 124\\
tracks, KRT finish rejected on merit) -\textgreater{} pour fan-in pass B + 9 rips -\textgreater{} 4 island-bond\\
vias -\textgreater{} `plane\_repair` (no repair needed: 0 split, 0 dead islands) -\textgreater{} gate.\\
`route\_cleanup` {*}{*}skipped{*}{*} - DRC was already 0/0 and its loop-breaker has regressed\\
twice on pour boards; nothing to gain, a real regression risk.\\
~\\
\#\# Three findings (all in LEARNINGS)\\
~\\
- {*}{*}`planes\_gen` rejects `\_note`.{*}{*} `\_PLANE\_KEYS` is a strict whitelist, so\\
  `constraints.planes{[}{]}` - which carries this file's most load-bearing note - cannot be\\
  fed to the documented step-0 invocation at all. Used planes-only sidecars\\
  (`kicad/planes\_p7.json`, `kicad/planes\_p7b.json`) instead of stripping the notes.\\
- {*}{*}A clean `--pad-window` does not predict Freerouting's width.{*}{*} All 61 power pads\\
  probed `ok` (R6.1/R8.1 reported 6.97/8.00 mm against a 2.055 mm floor); FR then routed\\
  those 0402 taps at {*}{*}0.8058 mm - the pad width{*}{*} - and necked +5V to 1.6348 (1210 pad)\\
  and +VIN to 1.4848 (0805 pad). 9 `track\_width` errors, fixed by pour fan-in per the\\
  remediation ladder step 4, not by necking or by weakening a rule.\\
- {*}{*}`planes\_gen`'s via grid can only be odd x odd.{*}{*} It is centroid-centred and\\
  pitch-stepped, so U1's 2.613 x 3.502 mm pad yields 3 x 3 = 9, never the 12 that fits.\\
  Hand-placed the 3 x 4 array with a half-pitch y stagger.\\
~\\
\#\# Judgment calls\\
~\\
- {*}{*}Power is poured, not trunked.{*}{*} +VIN (2 rects), +5V (3 rects) and /SW (2 rects) are\\
  F.Cu zones at priority above the GND pours. This is the only way to satisfy net-wide\\
  `aiee\_pwr\_width\_{*}` floors at 0402/0603 stubs without touching the `.kicad\_dru`. The\\
  `.kicad\_dru`, `.kicad\_pro` netclasses and `constraints.json` are byte-unchanged.\\
- {*}{*}All four GND planes kept solid; every track on F.Cu.{*}{*} `--power-layers` was forced to\\
  include B.Cu (the `auto` heuristic only ever considers INNER layers, so B.Cu would have\\
  been fair game for Freerouting and the second radiating face would have been cut).\\
- {*}{*}F.Cu GND uses thermal relief except where it must not.{*}{*} Board pour is priority 0\\
  thermal (J1/J2 screw terminals stay hand-solderable); a priority-3 `connect: solid`\\
  island covers U1's EP, PGND pin and C9's return, and two priority-4 solid patches clear\\
  the `starved\_thermal` on R1.2 / C3.2.\\
- {*}{*}M3 washer keepouts not added as rule areas.{*}{*} All four planes are GND, so a screw or\\
  washer bridging pour to pour is a GND-to-GND short. Verified instead that the nearest\\
  non-GND copper to each hole is 5.38 / 6.89 / 10.18 / 11.60 mm - all well past the\\
  3.25 mm washer radius. Flagged for P8 to confirm the reasoning rather than the rule.\\
~\\
\#\# Handed to P8\\
~\\
- 2 `/SW` tracks at exactly 2.31 mm survive inside the pour (FR's U1.8 -\textgreater{} L1.1 legs).\\
  Legal and load-bearing; they are counted in the 30.44 mm\textasciicircum{}2.\\
- The `/SW` bbox is 10.49 mm end to end because P6 put the BST cap, TP2 and the DNP\\
  snubber on the west side of the node. The switching current path is the 5.97 mm leg;\\
  the arm is 7.51 mm\textasciicircum{}2 of quiet tap copper. Judge the ceiling on area, which holds.\\
- `+5V`, `+VIN` fan-in pours mean check\_current will see pour necks, not tracks;\\
  `pour\_neck` only measures between via attachments and these pours are via-free.
\end{quote}
\paragraph*{P8}
\begin{quote}\small\ttfamily\raggedright
\# P8 Verification digest - sbuck-5v3a\\
~\\
Gates: `verify` PASS (0 failing, 2 waivers), `drc\_routed` PASS 0/0. 2 of 3 fix-loop\\
attempts used. Fresh-context review: 2 errors / 12 warnings, both errors FIXED.\\
~\\
\#\# The review found two errors that every gate had passed\\
~\\
- {*}{*}CRITICAL - D2's `K` cathode marker was on the ANODE end.{*}{*} Silk said pad 2\\
  (`/QGATE`); the cathode is pad 1 (`+VIN`). The netlist was always right. Fitted per\\
  that silk, the 15 V Zener reverses to a forward diode holding Vgs at -0.7 V, Q1\\
  never enhances, 2.6 A runs in its body diode at \textasciitilde{}2.1 W in an SO-8 - Q1 and the\\
  reverse-polarity protection both destroyed. Moved to (45.900, 59.000): 0.640 mm from\\
  pad 1, 3.036 mm from pad 2, agreeing with the footprint band and pin-1 dot.\\
- {*}{*}8 refdes labels named the wrong part{*}{*} (`silk\_misattributed` WARNINGS, so the\\
  error-only gate passed them). 8 fixed, 3 residual - at 1.0 mm text the label is\\
  2.6-3.2 mm wide against a 2.5-3.0 mm passive pitch, so no clean position exists.\\
~\\
\#\# Machine findings, and what they turned out to be\\
~\\
- `check\_thermal` L1: REAL. 100.7 mm\textasciicircum{}2 of +5V copper -\textgreater{} 48.10 C rise vs 45 allowed.\\
  Grew a +5V pour around L1's body -\textgreater{} 153.3 mm\textasciicircum{}2, {*}{*}42.51 C{*}{*}.\\
- `check\_current` GND x2: a MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT over three real defects. `pour\_neck`\\
  erodes each zone fill in isolation, so a pour split across zone objects reports a\\
  phantom 0.00 mm neck. Underneath were three genuine sub-2.055 mm via attachments in\\
  1.06-1.58 mm fingers. Repartitioned the zones; 3 unhomeable ring vias deleted.\\
- `check\_silk` x7: CHECKER DEFECT (check\_silk.py:172 buffers an unfilled circle into a\\
  filled disc). Waived, then the underlying rings were deleted at P9 anyway.\\
- `check\_pdn` x2: waived. Corrected reason - it never looks at the board, it filters\\
  decoupling.json and errors on an empty list, so it is a TRUE statement that no\\
  association named those rails. Coverage comes from check\_irdrop instead.\\
~\\
\#\# IR drop on the real copper (all three power nets)\\
~\\
\textbar{} Net \textbar{} I \textbar{} R \textbar{} worst drop \textbar{} jmax \textbar{}\\
\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}---\textbar{}\\
\textbar{} +VIN \textbar{} 2.60 A \textbar{} 5.36 mOhm \textbar{} 14.0 mV \textbar{} 2.65 A/mm \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} +5V \textbar{} 3.30 A \textbar{} 2.71 mOhm \textbar{} {*}{*}9.0 mV{*}{*} \textbar{} 2.41 A/mm \textbar{}\\
\textbar{} GND \textbar{} 3.30 A \textbar{} 0.34 mOhm \textbar{} {*}{*}1.1 mV{*}{*} \textbar{} 0.46 A/mm \textbar{}\\
~\\
`check\_pdn\_z` passes. Richardson deltas 0.03-0.05, so the grids converged.\\
~\\
\#\# Self-correction worth recording\\
~\\
Setting `pdn: false` on +5V and GND silenced check\_pdn's finding but ALSO excluded\\
both nets from check\_irdrop - the two highest-current nets on the board. Reverted and\\
waived instead: a waiver says "this check does not apply" without disabling unrelated\\
analysis.\\
~\\
\#\# Thermal, restated honestly\\
~\\
check\_thermal's "0.83 C headroom" on U1 is NOT a layout property: a\_eff measures\\
2137 mm\textasciicircum{}2 and clamps to A\_SAT 645, so theta is constant for any 4L board above\\
645 mm\textasciicircum{}2 - the 12 vias and three planes move it by 0.00 C. The believable figure is\\
the P1/P2 board ladder, corrected for 12 vias rather than 16 (2.16 -\textgreater{} 2.88 K/W):\\
{*}{*}Tj \textasciitilde{}98.7 C, margin 6.3 C{*}{*} against the 105 C design limit, with a +/-30\% band of\\
87.5-108.4 C. Spec floor is 125 C and abs max 150 C. The dominant lever is MOUNTING,\\
not layout - 53\% of cooling is radiation from two faces.
\end{quote}
\paragraph*{P9}
\begin{quote}\small\ttfamily\raggedright
\# P9 DFM digest - sbuck-5v3a\\
~\\
Gate `dfm`: {*}{*}PASS, 0 failing / 16 total{*}{*} (16 warnings), measured on gerbers\\
re-exported after the fixes. 1 of 3 fix-loop attempts used.\\
~\\
\#\# Two real findings, both invisible until the gerbers existed\\
~\\
{*}{*}1. Silk over the solder-mask opening, 7 test points, 0.1798 mm\textasciicircum{}2 each.{*}{*}\\
My diagnosis was WRONG and the fixer corrected it. I assumed an oversized mask\\
aperture (\textasciitilde{}0.92 mm radius). Measured: the aperture is {*}{*}1.7664 mm\textasciicircum{}2 = exactly\\
pi{*}0.75\textasciicircum{}2, zero mask expansion{*}{*}. The real cause is `lib/gerblib.py:read\_gerber`\\
approximating drawn arcs {*}{*}by their chord{*}{*} - KiCad exports a full circle as two\\
180-degree arcs, so both chords collapse onto the DIAMETER, a phantom 1.5 x 0.12 mm\\
bar through the pad centre. 0.1798 = 1.5 x 0.12 exactly.\\
My proposed fallback (enlarge the ring) {*}{*}could never have worked{*}{*} - the chord runs\\
through the centre at any radius. Deletion of the 7 decorative rings was the only\\
board-side fix. The signal-name labels, which carry the actual information, are untouched.\\
~\\
This is a SECOND false positive on the same innocent ring, from a DIFFERENT tool\\
defect than the P8 `check\_silk` one. {*}{*}Two checkers agreeing was not corroboration.{*}{*}\\
~\\
{*}{*}2. Copper clearance 0.0127 mm at (39.67, 51.05).{*}{*}\\
Both features were GND. The second was a {*}{*}0.0029 mm\textasciicircum{}2 crumb of the priority-0 board\\
pour{*}{*}, trapped in the 0.02 mm lane between zone 2's top (51.1) and the P8 Z2's bottom\\
(51.12). Mechanism: {*}{*}KiCad deburrs a pour at min\_thickness BEFORE subtracting\\
higher-priority zone outlines{*}{*}, so a sub-min\_thickness lane between two zone outlines\\
gets refilled and is never deburred away. The P8 "clears zone 2 by 0.02 mm" choice is\\
exactly what manufactured it. Fixed with a priority-6 GND bridge zone straddling the\\
seam; a second, longer 0.02 x 1.93 mm hair that nothing had flagged went with it.\\
F.Cu GND islands 5 -\textgreater{} 4. Min island gap 0.01267 -\textgreater{} {*}{*}0.1021 mm{*}{*}.\\
~\\
\#\# Fab package\\
~\\
`fab/`: gerbers + zip, drill, `BOM.csv` (21 rows), `CPL.csv` (29 rows),\\
`BOM-all.csv` / `CPL-all.csv` (unfiltered, for audit), `DNP-NOT-ASSEMBLED.txt`.\\
One rotation correction applied against JLCPCB's convention: {*}{*}Q1 SOIC-8, +270 deg{*}{*}.\\
`bom\_complete: true`, no missing LCSC codes.\\
~\\
{*}{*}DNP filtering was done BY HAND{*}{*} - no script in the pipeline reads a DNP mark, so\\
left alone JLC would have populated both hand-solder screw terminals and the snubber.\\
Excluded: J1, J2 (THT, hand-soldered on receipt per Q25), R9, C16 (snubber, populate\\
only if bring-up shows SW ringing).\\
~\\
\#\# Disclosed, deliberately NOT fixed\\
~\\
- Two residual etch slivers (0.05 x 1.71 mm and 0.078 x 0.497 mm), fused to\\
  neighbouring copper so no gate fires, but a fab may query them.\\
- {*}{*}Min F.Cu island gap is 0.1021 mm against JLC's 0.1016 floor - 0.5 um of margin.{*}{*}\\
  Pre-existing and unchanged by this work, but it means ANY further pour edit risks\\
  tripping `dfm\_clearance`. The risk of touching exceeds the risk of leaving.\\
- 16 dfm warnings remain (15 pin-1 dot slivers + 1 silk width), unchanged.\\
~\\
\#\# Script defects found, recorded not fixed (skill work belongs in its own session)\\
~\\
- `lib/gerblib.py` chords drawn arcs - the S12 `approximate\_arcs` fix reached\\
  `\_flash\_polys` only. {*}{*}Every footprint drawing a silk ring around a pad will fail\\
  the dfm gate forever{*}{*} until this is fixed in the tool.\\
- `planes\_gen` should refuse or warn when a planned region edge lands within\\
  `min\_thickness` of an existing same-layer zone outline - fully detectable at plan time.\\
- No script owns footprint-internal silk on a placed board.
\end{quote}
